name: Private payment + side effect (2 rounds)
tagline: Bank B pays Bank A in its own ZK deposits and receives a bond — atomic, one settlement tx, no Atom, no shared lane
concept: The minimal private 'pay + side effect' pattern. Cash is Bank B's own tokenised deposit as a Zeto (ZK) token: amounts are hidden from everyone but the two banks. The side effect — here a bond position — lives in a private contract inside a BILATERAL Pente group that only Bank A and Bank B are members of. Bank B locks the cash with the group itself as the delegate, so the group's single settle() transaction can move the bond AND release the cash as one base-ledger transaction (a Pente external call): all-or-nothing, without deploying an Atom and without any shared group that other bank pairs queue behind. Each bank pair is its own lane — which is what lets this scale with the number of banks, until the shared chain's execution rate becomes the limit.

steps.title: Set up: Bank B's deposit token + a bilateral A⇄B group
steps.plain: Bank B issues its own tokenised deposits as a Zeto (ZK) token and mints 25,000 to itself. Bank A and Bank B form a two-member Pente privacy group and deploy a small settlement contract in it that holds Bank A's 1,000 bond units. Bank C runs a node on the same chain but is in neither.

steps.title: Round 1 (in parallel): Bank B escrows the cash to the group and bids
steps.plain: Bank B locks 10,000 of its deposits with the GROUP as the only party allowed to release them, and — in the same round — records inside the group that it is buying 400 units under this trade id. Two base-ledger transactions, sent in parallel; the chain sees a Zeto lock and an opaque group transition, no amounts.
steps.tech: cash.lock(10,000, delegate=group) · 0.6 s · 346k gas   ‖   group.bid(tradeId, 400) · 0.6 s · 144k gas

steps.title: Bank B prepares the payment (ZK proof, nothing on chain)
steps.plain: Bank B's node builds the zero-knowledge proof for 'pay the locked 10,000 to Bank A' as a prepared transaction — not submitted. It hands the encoded call to Bank A, who can check the output it would receive before agreeing (that check is off-chain and not modelled here).

steps.title: Bank A settles — bond and cash move in ONE transaction
steps.plain: Bank A calls settle() inside the group: the contract checks Bank B's bid, moves 400 bond units from A to B in the private register, and emits the prepared cash transfer as a Pente external call. Pente executes it in the same base-ledger transaction as the group's state change — if the cash leg failed, the bond move would revert too. Only A and B can see either leg; Bank C sees an opaque transaction.
steps.tech: group.settle(tradeId, 400, cash, transferLocked) → Zeto.transferLocked(→bankA) in-tx · 0.8 s · 457k gas · one tx: true
